passages.text: Diana has been an advocate for children, teachers and our public education system for many years. She grew up in her district and went to Winegard, Walker Middle and Oak Ridge High School. She has been an employee, as well as a citizen advocate. Teachers speak up for children because they don't have their own organized group so as a teacher, we know a teacher's working conditions are a child's learning conditions. They deserve a qualified and certified teacher with the training and knowledge of child development as well as the state standards, combined with a growing "toolbelt" that they build throughout their career working with students.

1) Safety -Students and employees need to know they are safe each and every day in their learning environment. We currently have a School Resource Officer on every campus in OCPS. We can always improve the security of our campuses.​

2) Choice - Ask parents and students why they are moving to other learning options? Is it the security? Is it the focus on high-stakes testing? Is it the discipline and bullying that goes unchecked? We should survey parents and students for their needs and combine that information with teacher and administrator training and research to think outside of the box from the traditional brick and mortar we have always known and find other options to keep students learning in our public schools. We have lots of choices like Magnet programs, Career Technical Education offering certificates for culinary services, firefighting, beauty industry, etc. Magnet programs with a focus on STEM or finance.
We can do a better job of advertising these options to the community and work to add additional ideas like micros schools. We can look for solutions together.​

3) Professional Pay for Professional Work- Florida is ranked 50th in pay. How can we attract and keep the best talent in our schools if we don't pay a competitive salary? I can read the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report and look for the programs or "fat" in the budget. While losing students means we must cut back, we can find solutions to pay our employees a living wage plus raise pay so they stay and make OCPS the A district that it is and realize that it is an A district based on the hard work of 24,000 employees who work to make students successful every day.

4) Transparency, Integrity and a Culture that doesn't threaten the livelihood of employees who speak up . I am personally aware of the many stories and the broken "Whistleblower Process" in Orange County. I will ask for a Work Session to bring these concerns to light and improve the working conditions so that employees don't feel afraid to speak up. It is collaboration that is the core of a Professional Learning Committee and teachers are often not able to speak up.​

5) Solutions, not excuses -I watch the School Board meetings and started a Facebook page for the community to join me as the School Board Members make decisions about the policies and actions going forward. Often, I see school board members, vote on a "consent agenda" with little to no questioning or offering of solutions. They should rely on the staff through the Superintendent for those day-to-day operations, but there are several issues that need more review.
A. We need to honestly review the research on the 1 to 1 computer devices and get feedback from teachers, parents and students on the current model.

B. Ask staff for solutions. Maurice Draggon cut thousands of dollars in repair expenses by moving the laptops to a leasing corporation that included the repair personnel and cut our costs. Let's encourage the staff when they come up with such solutions with recognition and financial incentives.
Let's all work for solutions and stop making excuses for the students leaving and the teachers leaving so we can have a true A plus district.

*Disclaimer. There are great things happening in classrooms and schools every day. We don't hear about them enough. Let's do a better at celebrating successes and looking for solutions when something is not working but always, ask the employees for their input. They are a resource and world of knowledge we often ignore in surveys. This is my reason for running to represent the families and employees of District 3 but all families and employees of Orange County Public School going forward. I will be an activist for public education and the rights of students in public education. I came back to give back where I began my journey. I humbly ask for your vote for District 3

passages.heading: A PASSION FOR EDUCATION
passages.text: Education has always been my passion. I have spent over a decade in various roles within our school system, from classroom teacher to community organizer. My experiences have shaped my understanding of our district's needs. I am dedicated to ensuring every child has access to a quality education. Join me as we create a brighter future for our students and our community. Vote on August 18th or go to an Early voting location.

passages.heading: Empowerment Through Education
passages.text: My mission is to empower every student and family in District 3. I believe that every child deserves the opportunity to succeed, regardless of their background. Through collaboration with parents, educators, and local organizations, we can develop innovative solutions that address the diverse needs of our students. Together, let's make a difference!
